text:
ashley: Heads-up — scheduling a quick sync about dedicated capacity tradeoffs for Q3 roadmap. Focus: surge attenuation (burst thresholds), lease phasing (commit windows), and autoscale gating. Who's available?

kevin: +1. We need clearer SLOs for burst fallbacks. Can we define max continuous burst time vs short spikes? :thinking_face:

pritam: From runtime side, we can support two burst modes: soft (prioritized queues) and hard (preemptible slots). Need policy for when to promote soft->hard.

eva: Customer ask from AeroHealth: want guaranteed 5k rps for 10m bursts per month. Need SLA wording and examples of how that maps to reserved pools.

ashley: Quick strawman: introduce "burst buckets" per reserved pool. Each bucket = GPU-seconds. Customers purchase buckets (monthly). Unused buckets expire at month-end. Buckets are consumed when autoscale launches extra workers.

kevin: Buckets map nicely to billing. Two follow-ups: 1) allow a one-time carryover flag for Enterprise; 2) define a per-tenant max-sustained-window to avoid slow leaks. Ops complexity will increase but manageable.

pritam: Implementation notes: runtime will track pool_kv[bucket_id] and per-tenant usage. We'll add a Prom metric: `dedicated_pool_burst_used{pool_id,tenant}` and alert at 75%/90%. Also need an API: POST /pools/:id/burst-alloc to deduct buckets atomically.

eva: Proposed launch criteria (must-haves):
- API surface to configure burst_bucket_size, carryover (bool), and per-tenant burst caps
- Metrics & a Console dashboard per-pool showing bucket usage and heatmap
- Documented pricing examples and customer-facing FAQ
- E2E canary with 1 pilot customer and rollback plan

ashley: Autoscale gating rules idea: below 50% burst remaining -> restrict opportunistic (best-effort) tenants; above 80% -> allow opportunistic bursts; between 50-80% -> allow limited headroom. Also set a minimum reserve for baseline traffic.

kevin: Edge cases to flag: overlapping bursts across tenants on same GPU host; eviction correctness when multiple priorities collide; and fairshare when multiple customers have similar commitments. I suggest eviction priority: (1) non-committed opportunistic, (2) soft-burst committed, (3) hard commitments. Use commit-level then signup timestamp as tie-breaker.

pritam: Runtime pseudocode for gating (rough):
```python
# pool.burst_remaining in GPU-seconds
if pool.burst_remaining < pool.burst_size * 0.5:
    throttle(opportunistic_tenants)
elif pool.burst_remaining > pool.burst_size * 0.8:
    allow(opportunistic_tenants)
else:
    allow_limited(burst_qps=pool.base_qps * 1.5)
```
Note: we'll also enforce per-tenant sustained_window checks (e.g., max 10m sustained at N QPS).

eva: Created ticket for billing/carryover details: RID-452 (ops will own pricing language).

ops-bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RID-452

ashley: Next steps: Kevin -> prototype alert thresholds and dashboard wireframe; Pritam -> draft runtime RFC with eviction rules & APIs; Eva -> scope AeroHealth pilot and draft SLA language. Sync Thurs 11am. @kevin @pritam @eva :thumbsup:

kevin: Sounds good. I'll put a draft alert dashboard on the Product board today.

pritam: Will start the RFC and link to the ticket. Expect first draft by Wed EOD.

eva: I'll confirm AeroHealth availability for the pilot and collect their traffic profile.

ashley: Thanks team — aim for an actionable RFC + pilot plan by next week.
